problemStatement: The trade reconciliation batch job that settles daily equity and fixed-income trades runs as a single-file .NET Framework 4.8 console application (TradeReconciler.exe) on an out-of-support Windows Server 2012 R2 host. The framework is end-of-life for security patching, the host cannot be re-imaged without a hardware refresh, and no engineer on the current team has production experience with WCF or the legacy MSMQ input adapter it depends on. Operations wants the reconciliation behavior preserved exactly while the runtime moves onto a supported, cross-platform .NET 8 target that the team can operate and extend.
goals: Port TradeReconciler.exe to .NET 8 with feature parity for all currently exercised reconciliation paths.
Remove the WCF/MSMQ dependency in favor of a supported file-drop input adapter without changing the on-disk trade file format.
Make the reconciliation engine unit-testable (it is currently untested) without changing its externally observable matching behavior.
Restore engineering's ability to safely patch and deploy the service on supported infrastructure.
nonGoals: Changing the trade matching algorithm's tolerances or business rules.
Adding new reconciliation report types beyond the two currently produced (matched.csv, exceptions.csv).
Containerization or cloud migration of the host (tracked separately).
successMetrics: 100% of the 12 golden regression trade files reproduce byte-identical matched.csv and exceptions.csv output versus the legacy binary.
Reconciliation engine reaches at least 90% branch coverage under automated unit tests (currently 0%).
Batch run completes within 110% of the legacy binary's wall-clock time for the 250k-row benchmark file.
Zero dependency on WCF, MSMQ, or .NET Framework-only APIs in the ported codebase.
stakeholders: Trade Operations (owns the daily reconciliation run and sign-off on output parity)
Platform Engineering (owns the hosting environment and patching cadence)
Compliance (requires evidence that settlement behavior did not change)
Engineering Lead for Reconciliation Services (technical approver)
